Question: In the \(xy\)-plane, the segment with endpoints \((-5,0)\) and \((25,0)\) is the diameter of a circle. If the point \((x,15)\) is on the circle, then \(x=\)
Solution:
The center is the midpoint of the diameter, so it is
\[
\left(\frac{-5+25}{2},0\right)=(10,0).
\]
The diameter has length \(25-(-5)=30\), giving radius \(15\).

The point \((x,15)\) is already \(15\) units vertically above the center. If \(x\ne10\), the horizontal and vertical displacements form the legs of a right triangle. By the Pythagorean theorem, its distance from the center would satisfy
\[
\text{distance}^2=(x-10)^2+15^2>15^2.
\]
That would exceed the radius, so the point could not be on the circle.

Therefore \(x=10\). The point \((10,15)\) is indeed exactly \(15\) units from the center, so \(\boxed{x=10}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
